facts.fact: Neela keeps a cache in a cleft of rock under the second spur: a day cloth, a shawl and a water gourd, hidden after she collapsed beside Devan's bed in ch13, so she can turn back away from the ledge.
facts.why: needed because the beat has her turn back among the rocks and walk home.

facts.fact: The two raider scouts keep a cold camp (no fire) on the lip above the shelf in the lower narrows, with bows and a wrapped bronze signal mirror meant to flash the patrol's count to others beyond the cut. Who waits beyond is not known.
facts.why: needed because the beat specifies scouts, bows and a mirror waiting for dawn.

facts.fact: The scouts carry newly struck Varanad silver (sprig on one face, sharp milled edge, never handled) and a forged split-ash tally with real council wax that smells of clove. Devan notes the coins are unspent and takes the satchel and coin as evidence.
A scout's knife cuts a thin line across Neela's shoulder in leopard shape; it reopens as she turns back and she bleeds a little.
facts.why: gives the kill a cost; a minor wound that is not tied to later plot.

facts.fact: Valli (Ammu) did not come to the gate on the day after the fever broke, though Neela expected her ('tomorrow').
facts.why: continuity with ch13's jackal call; leaves Ammu's absence as an open question.

facts.fact: The 'pepper-store cat' is the fort's notched ginger tom, which Devan feeds. Janu says it has caught nothing since 'the fever year'.
facts.why: needed for the supper line in the beat.

facts.fact: Devan's patrol numbers eleven riders, and Raman's death in spring happened in single file under the shelf in the lower narrows.
facts.why: gives Devan a reason to insist on riding.
